sections.h2: Who handles your Union County tax bill
sections.html:
Two offices matter. Tax Administration oversees property tax, and its Revenue Division sends and collects the bills. Find the Revenue Division in Monroe at 500 N. Main Street, Suite 119, phone 704-283-3848, or write to P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111-0038.

For a question about your value, or to appeal it, contact the Tax Administrator's Office, Suite 236 in the same building, 704-283-3746. Paying by hand? The collector's counter inside the Government Center takes payments Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

Ten towns let the county bill for them as well: Fairview, Hemby Bridge, Lake Park, Marshville, Marvin, Mineral Springs, Stallings, Waxhaw, Wesley Chapel and Wingate. If your house is inside one, you receive one combined bill from the county. A parcel in any other town needs a quick call to find out who sends its bill.

Union County is one of the faster-growing places in the state. Its July 2025 population estimate is 267,674, which is 12.4% higher than the April 2020 base, spread over 632.74 square miles of land (376.6 people per square mile).

Owned homes have a median value of $417,300, and 81.6% are lived in by their owners. Housing units total 95,683 and builders pulled 2,707 permits for 2025. Median rent is $1,496, and median household income is $102,900. All that growth means your assessed value may look quite different from what you paid.

The latest countywide reappraisal lifted taxable value from $32.38 billion (2021) to $60.05 billion at the January 1, 2025 valuation date. That is a 60.05% jump. Homes gained 63.45%, while commercial and industrial property gained 45.59%.

The parcel count rose from 104,057 to 114,182, and the median home value went from $293,377 to $403,000.

In the years between reappraisals, you only get a new notice if the property itself changes: new construction, an addition, a teardown, a remodel, a rezoning or a change in acreage. State law sets reappraisal at least every eighth year, so ask Tax Administration when the next one is due.

Real and personal property bills are payable from September 1. You can wait through January 5 without penalty, and a check postmarked by then counts as on time. If that date is a Saturday or Sunday, you get until Monday.

Beginning January 6, a 2% charge applies for the rest of the month, followed by three-fourths of 1% each month thereafter. Car and truck tax is paid when you register or renew the tag, so it is not part of this bill.

Call the office for this year's rate and ask whether a prepayment discount applies.

sections.h2: Other charges the Revenue Division collects
sections.html:
The division handles more than property tax. Your closing agent may ask about any of the following for the house you are selling.

  • Bills on land, buildings, and business or personal property.
  • Delinquent motor vehicle tax bills.
  • Gross receipts taxes.
  • Current and delinquent water and sewer bills.
  • Landfill fees and other utility payments.

The division also values every registered motor vehicle owned by a county resident. Phone 704-283-3848 to find out whether the property carries an open water, sewer or landfill balance.

Union County accepts payment five ways.

  • Mail: use the return envelope or write to P.O. Box 38, Monroe, NC 28111.
  • Drop box: on Stewart St. Extension, behind the Historic Post Office.
  • Phone: 1-855-497-0718.
  • Web: the county's pay online link.
  • Counter: the Government Center.

At a sale, your closing agent can settle the current bill so the property passes to the buyer free of tax debt. Have the closer ask the Revenue Division for a payoff number.

Your first stop is an informal review with Tax Administration. If that does not settle it, request a formal hearing before the county's equalization board. A staff appraiser reviews what you submit and mails a written decision. Return the form printed at the foot of that letter and the case moves up to the board.

Five local citizens sit on the board, listen to you and to the staff, and rule within 30 days. Still disagree? The board's letter lays out the next step, the statewide Property Tax Commission, and G.S. 105-290 allows 30 days from the mailing date of that notice.

Evidence that helps: appraisals as of the revaluation date, sales of similar properties, photos of unusual damage, and letters about septic limits from Environmental Health or a soil scientist. The percentage of change since a prior assessment cannot be considered. Neither stage costs a fee, and hiring a lawyer is optional. Windows to file follow the mailing of notices, so call Tax Administration to learn the dates that apply now.

sections.h2: Programs that can reduce what you owe
sections.html:
An owner can pick one of three state programs to shrink a bill, never more than one. Apply to the county assessor using Form AV-9. On the 2026 form, the income limit is $38,800 and the upper circuit breaker band is $58,200.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion, G.S. 105-277.1.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion, G.S. 105-277.1C, with no age or income cap.
  • Circuit breaker, G.S. 105-277.1B: tax is held to a share of income and the rest is deferred as a lien.

Ask Tax Administration which one fits and when to file. A sale ends eligibility for the circuit breaker, so deferred taxes become payable at closing.

sections.h2: A short checklist before you list
sections.html:
Pull your latest bill and confirm whether you pay it yourself or through a lender's escrow account. Look up whether the parcel sits inside one of the ten towns, because that changes who sends the bill. Phone the Revenue Division for a balance on any water, sewer or landfill account. If you think your value is too high, gather comparable sales and photos before you call Tax Administration, since the evidence is what moves a reviewer. Then tell your closer which relief program, if any, you currently use, so a deferred amount is not a surprise at settlement.

The Government Center is the one building you may need for most of this, since the tax offices and the collector's counter are both there, so a single trip can cover a payoff request, a question about a value and a payment. Give yourself time. A payoff request to the Revenue Division is simple, but the closer needs the number before the settlement statement is drawn up, and a bank or the mail can add days. Starting a week or two ahead of the closing date keeps the sale on schedule.

sections.h2: If tax is still due when you sell
sections.html:
Unpaid tax travels with the parcel. G.S. 105-355 puts a lien on it from the listing date, adding penalties, interest and costs, and that is why a buyer's lender will insist on payoff at the closing table.

A long-unpaid bill can end in a foreclosure suit (G.S. 105-374) and an auction held at the courthouse door. You can still redeem ahead of confirmation by paying the tax plus the added penalties, interest and costs.

Order a payoff from the Revenue Division, have the closer send it from your sale proceeds, and hold on to the receipt. Deed stamp tax is its own charge against the seller, taken by the register of deeds when the deed is filed.

With a cash buyer there is no lender underwriting or appraisal to wait on. Taxes still get paid from your proceeds, so request the number early and hand it to your closer. Raise utility balances in the same call, because those can hold up a closing if they surface late.

faqs.q: When does Union County need my tax payment?
faqs.a: Due September 1. Interest stays off until January 6, when 2% applies for the month, and three-fourths of 1% is added monthly after that.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Union County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Use the collector's counter at the Government Center, open weekdays 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. Mailed payments go to the Monroe post office box.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Union County value?
faqs.a: Yes. An informal review with Tax Administration comes first, and an equalization board hearing is next if needed. Call 704-283-3746 for dates.

faqs.q: Does Union County have a veteran property tax exclusion?
faqs.a: Yes, for a qualifying disabled veteran: the first $45,000 of value is excluded. Apply through the county assessor.

faqs.q: Who owes deed stamp tax on a Union County sale?
faqs.a: Seller pays it, at the register's office before the deed is recorded. Check the settlement statement for the amount.
